svg.title: The pictures of a visual change
svg.desc: The maintainer or a bot pushes to a pull request that changes how something looks, and its visual check renders the pictures again and keeps each one that looks different in an artifact, before and after, with its report, which says of each whether the eye sees its change. When the check passed, the pager asks GitHub for the pull request, with a token of its app. One of someone else, from a fork, that moved on to a newer head, or of a bot that merges by itself ends there, and so does a head whose pictures went already. Otherwise the pager reads the artifact with the same token, through the short-lived address of its storage. When every picture looks as committed, nothing comes. When the eye sees none of the changes, one quiet line comes, with how many pictures differ and by how much at most. When it sees some, their message goes into the topic of its release, or of a thing of their own, and the album of the three largest changes that the eye sees follows, each as one comparison of the same frame before and after with the changes framed in red, once per pull request: a newer head edits the message in place. The merge or the end of the pull request ticks the topic off.
